A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 19 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v4, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original query-answering experiments on FB15k237 and Hetionet, including ranking results, parameter sensitivity, runtime measurements, and a qualitative example.

after.justification: v4 retains these experiments and adds preference-partition validation, evaluation on curated preferences, additional failure examples, and LLM timing results.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the Cosine and NQR updates and RankNet objective. However, v2 Table 5 describes attention, pooling, and a scalar tanh output, whereas v4 Table 7 specifies a 1003-to-256-to-2 MLP with sigmoid outputs. Because v2's appendix already conflicts with its main text, the PDFs do not establish whether the underlying architecture changed or its documentation was corrected.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FB15k237, Hetionet, and the same 14 query structures. v4 additionally tests 140 FB15k237 queries with LLM-proposed, human-approved preference partitions, extending evaluation beyond purely embedding-derived preferences.

E2.justification: The ranking comparisons retain Unconstrained/QTO, LightGBM, Cosine, and NQR. v4 additionally compares LLM clustering runtime with reranking runtimes in Section 7, although the tasks and inputs differ. Rocchio is discussed only as related work.

E3.justification: Appendix D revises the reported Cosine search from two positive coefficient grids to alpha in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} and beta in {-0.5, 0, 0.5}, and removes NQR margin/KL search settings. New protocols cover human approval of ten queries per structure, partition-agreement measurement, and LLM timing. Original benchmark splits and feedback-step ranges remain unchanged; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v4 adds a substantial check of the synthetic-preference assumption: agreement with human-approved partitions and reranking evaluation using those partitions in Appendix B and E.1. Table 3 also adds five incorrectly demoted answers and their rank drops. The earlier Cosine sensitivity analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 95% confidence intervals and a paired t-test for Cosine versus NQR runtime. v4 extends confidence-interval reporting to added results without specifying changed run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimators, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v4 adds 79.04% partition agreement, curated results such as Cosine pairwise accuracy of 89.84% and NQR MRR of 23.39%, LLM clustering time of 3.5 seconds, and incorrect-demotion results. All 360 metric entries in v2 Tables 6–7 remain identical in v4 Tables 8–9, as do Table 2 runtimes. The genuine per-interaction NDCG curves from v2's main figure disappear.

T1.justification: Section 4 replaces the informal soft-constraint definition with a Boolean predicate and a constrained answer set. It adds explicit inequalities expressing preservation of logical answers and preference ordering. The method equations and loss remain equivalent, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain interactive query answering with soft constraints, two lightweight rerankers, and generated preference benchmarks. Added abstract and conclusion wording reiterates the existing interaction paradigm and benchmark contribution rather than changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds an external-validity argument that synthetic preference evaluations predict behavior on curated preferences, and attributes some difficulty to imperfect clusters. It expands the explanation of similarity propagation harming correct answers and discusses LLM applicability limits involving textual access and computational cost.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a code link, the GPT-5.1 partition-generation prompt, annotation guidelines, and the curation procedure. Appendix D substantially revises the architecture and tuning documentation to agree more closely with Section 5. The PyTorch, A100, and 120GB RAM information is relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v4 adds Rocchio's relevance-feedback work and distinguishes query-vector updates from score-based reranking. It adds Reimers and Gurevych, Grand et al., and Merkx et al. to support embedding-based similarity, plus Vaswani et al. for the LLM discussion. Existing CQA and learning-to-rank positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Section 4 is rewritten, terminology and notation receive corrections, and Section 6.4 is absorbed into Section 6.3 and Appendix D. Additional discussion and Appendix E.1 extend the narrative, while most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds an NQR schematic and curated-study displays, expands the qualitative table with demotions, and replaces the architecture table. The main performance figure changes from four metric columns to three: v2's H@10 curves reappear labeled NDCG@10 in v4 Figure 4, while the original NDCG panels are omitted.

improvement.justification: Human-approved preference validation, explicit failure evidence, and more consistent implementation documentation address important weaknesses in v2. However, v4 Figure 4 mislabels the former H@10 curves as NDCG@10, and the expanded discussion makes NDCG claims inconsistent with the retained evidence. These material benefits and reporting harms leave the overall net quality direction unclear.
